scope: two preselected SWE-bench train failures; opt-in same-assertion red-green probe experiment

cases.observation: The frozen probe checked only convert_encodings(['Not Supplied']) == ['iso8859']; it turned green, but all three official target tests still failed.
The Agent first edited at step 11, then attempted two probes without a pre-edit red baseline; the opt-in red-green gate rejected those probes, although the official patch passed.

conclusion: The mechanism enforces a genuine same-assertion red-green transition. Official resolution was 1/2, but neither trajectory passed both official and strict Agent-quality gates, so the accepted train corpus is unchanged.
limitations: One stochastic sample per task and an unpinned provider revision do not establish a causal improvement over earlier 0/2 runs.
A red-green probe can be too narrow; it does not replace issue-target or regression tests.
A patch can be officially resolved even if the opt-in pre-edit probe protocol was not followed.
The new initial prompt does not exactly match earlier failed trajectories, so this run cannot create a valid same-prompt preference pair with them.
Official target tests were used only for post-hoc grading, not shown to the Agent.
